text:
Sam R.: Quick RFC follow-up — proposing an "API retrofit safety-net" for the v3->v4 migration. High level: accept both shapes at the gateway for a bounded period, attach a compat header, and run a tiny, well-tested transformer pipeline in the router so the runtime only ever sees v4. Reason: avoid client 400s while we chase down slow migrating tenants.

Ravi: I get the intent, but worried about extra latency and CPU in the gateway. Even small transforms add tail latency. Do we have a budget?

Sam R.: Good point. Target: <1ms p50 added, <3ms p99. Transformer runs in C++ fast-path (same process as route matching) and only for sampled requests + tenants opted-in. Default path is native v4.

Kelsey: Instead of sniffing payload shapes, can we rely on a capability header clients set? Cleaner and cheaper for router.

Sam R.: Yes — prefer capability header for new clients. But we need a fallback for older clients that won't change quickly. Plan: 1) Accept X-Redwood-Client-Capabilities header if present. 2) Otherwise, do a cheap shape-hint (first 64 bytes only) and if ambiguous, sample + telemetry for rollback.

Elaine: How do we avoid cache fragmentation? Our CDN/edge caches are keyed by path+headers. If we add compat header we might double cache entries.

Matt: We can normalize cache keys in the transform stage and emit a canonical cache-key header for downstream caches (Cache-Key: /v4/...). That keeps cache hit-rates stable. Also we can route transforms to local LRU for hot tenants.

devops-bot: new deploy pipeline note: "Router: add transform-hook v1" queued (deploy window 03/05 02:00 UTC).

Sam R.: Example envoy-like config prototype: 
```
- match: /api/*
  transforms:
    - name: retrofit-v3-to-v4
      when: header_present(X-Redwood-Client-Capabilities) == false
      sample_rate: 0.02
      fast_path: true
      emit_header: X-RW-Compat: retrofit-v3-to-v4
      canonical_cache_key: true
```

Ravi: Sampling only 2% initially — good. How do we decide when to flip to 100% or to start rejecting v3? Need concrete rollout criteria.

Sam R.: Proposed rollout gates:
- Stage 0 (trial): sample 2% and log metrics; owners: Sam + Kelsey
- Stage 1 (canary): opt-in tenants -> 25% transform for those tenants; monitor for 24h
- Stage 2 (ramp): 100% transform for opt-in tenants + 5% global sample
- Stage 3 (coexist): full transform for all, emit deprecation header to clients
- Stage 4 (sunset): after 6 months and <0.1% conversion errors, return 400 for untagged v3 requests

Kelsey: Add clear telemetry dimensions: tenant_id, transform-version, conversion-failure, p50/p99 added latency. Also track delta in request sizes (to catch accidental payload blowup).

Elaine: Who owns the migration runbook & tenant outreach? Product should notify high-usage tenants. Suggest Elaine + Matt coordinating with CSM.

Sam R.: Agreed. Action items:
- Sam + Kelsey: land transform API and config in router (PR target: next week)
- Matt: add cache-key normalization + LRU plan (PR target: two weeks)
- Elaine: draft tenant comms and a list of top-50 clients to contact
- Ravi: perf test harness for transform overhead (due in 5 days)

Matt: One more operational safety net — add a kill-switch flag per-tenant in the control plane so we can opt-out transforms instantly if we see regressions.

Sam R.: Yep — global + per-tenant kill-switches included. We'll also emit a telemetry event to the incident pipeline when transform-failure-rate > 0.5% for 5m.

Ravi: Sounds reasonable. If perf tests pass I'm +1. Small nit: let's call it "retrofit" in docs to avoid overloading the word "shim".

Kelsey: LGTM. I'll help with tests.

Sam R.: Thanks all — I'll convert these notes to a short follow-up RFC and attach the config prototype. Will also schedule a 30m sync with product/CS tomorrow. :thumbsup:
